Smogon\'s tiering system is the global standard for competitive singles Pokémon battles. Its primary goal is to create a balanced environment where as many Pokémon as possible can be played competitively.
With the exception of Ubers and Anything Goes, most tiers are usage-based: the more a Pokémon is used in a higher tier, the higher it ranks in the hierarchy.
Smogon organizes Pokémon into playability tiers so lower-powered Pokémon do not have to compete against overpowered legendaries.
These tiers apply specifically to competitive Singles formats hosted on Pokémon Showdown.

1. AG (Anything Goes) — virtually no restrictions besides the 6-Pokémon team limit. Home to specimens too powerful even for Ubers (e.g. Mega Rayquaza, Calyrex-Shadow) and mechanics banned elsewhere.

2. Uber — historically the banlist for OU. The battleground for major legendaries and over-centralizing threats (Kyogre, Koraidon, Miraidon, Zacian...).

3. OU (OverUsed) — the benchmark tier. Smogon's flagship format, used for most official tournaments. Top-tier non-legendaries and balanced legendaries (Landorus-Therian, Kingambit, Iron Valiant...).

4. UU (UnderUsed) — Pokémon below OU's usage threshold (~4.52%) but still strong competitive options: powerful niche attackers or Pokémon outcompeted by current OU trends.

5. RU (RarelyUsed) — below UU, for Pokémon that lack the versatility or power for UU.

6. NU (NeverUsed) — below RU, Pokémon often overlooked in higher divisions.

7. PU — the lowest official usage-based tier (named after "P.U.", a bad smell), still a highly competitive and complex metagame.

8. ZU (Zero Used) — an unofficial tier below PU, giving the remaining Pokémon their own competitive metagame.
The boundary to stay in a tier is roughly 4.52%, meaning a Pokémon must appear on at least 1 in every 22 teams in that tier\'s ladder.
A Pokémon in a lower tier (e.g. NU) can always be used in a higher tier (e.g. OU), but higher-tier Pokémon cannot drop into lower tiers.

Between main tiers exist intermediate categories called BL (e.g. UUBL, RUBL, NUBL, PUBL). A Pokémon is placed in UUBL if it was banned from UU for being too strong, but doesn\'t have high enough usage to be officially classified as OU — it can\'t be used in UU, but is legal in OU.

1. Quarterly usage updates — every three months, Smogon analyzes battle statistics from Pokémon Showdown. Pokémon exceeding the usage threshold move up, underused ones drop down.\n\n2. Suspect tests & quickbans — if a Pokémon, move, or ability overpowers a tier, the council runs a community vote (Suspect Test) or quickbans it to the tier above.
Borderline categories are purely banlists for lower tiers, not playable metagames with their own ladders.
Suspect tests require players to achieve a high skill rating (GXE) on a fresh ladder account to earn voting rights.
